sanskrit: yām eva rātriṃ śatrughna parṇaśālāṃ samāviśat tām eva rātriṃ sītāpi prasūtā dārakadvayam
english: That very same night on which Śatrughna entered the leaf-hut, that very same night Sītā too gave birth to a pair of boys.

sanskrit: tato 'rdharātrasamaye bālakā munidārakāḥ vālmīkeḥ priyam ācakhyuḥ sītāyāḥ prasavaṃ śubham tasya rakṣāṃ mahātejaḥ kuru bhūtavināśinīm
english: Then, at the middle of the night, the young disciples of the sage joyfully announced to Vālmīki the auspicious birth of Sītā's children: "O mighty one, perform for them the protective rite that dispels evil spirits."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā munir harṣam upāgamat bhūtaghnīṃ cākarot tābhyāṃ rakṣāṃ rakṣovināśinīm
english: Hearing those words of theirs, the sage was filled with joy; and he performed for those two a protective rite with the demon-slaying, demon-destroying charm.

sanskrit: kuśamuṣṭim upādāya lavaṃ caiva tu sa dvijaḥ vālmīkiḥ pradadau tābhyāṃ rakṣāṃ bhūtavināśinīm
english: Taking a handful of kuśa grass and a blade of lava grass as well, the twice-born Vālmīki bestowed upon the two of them the protection that destroys evil spirits.

sanskrit: yas tayoḥ pūrvajo jātaḥ sa kuśair mantrasaṃskṛtaiḥ nirmārjanīyas tu bhavet kuśa ity asya nāmataḥ
english: The one of the two born first was to be cleansed with kuśa grass consecrated by sacred mantras; and from this, his name shall be Kuśa.

sanskrit: yaś cāparo bhavet tābhyāṃ lavena susamāhitaḥ nirmārjanīyo vṛddhābhir lavaś ceti sa nāmataḥ
english: And the other of the two, to be carefully cleansed by the elder women with a blade of lava grass — he shall bear the name Lava.

sanskrit: evaṃ kuśalavau nāmnā tāv ubhau yamajātakau matkṛtabhyāṃ ca nāmabhyāṃ khyātiyuktau bhaviṣyataḥ
english: Thus those two, born as twins, shall be known by the names Kuśa and Lava — the two names bestowed by me — and they shall attain great renown.

sanskrit: te rakṣāṃ jagṛhus tāṃ ca munihastāt samāhitāḥ akurvaṃś ca tato rakṣāṃ tayor vigatakalmaṣāḥ
english: Those pure-souled ones, composed and reverent, received the protective ritual from the sage's hand, and then those blameless ones duly performed the protective rite for the two infants.

sanskrit: tathā tāṃ kriyamāṇāṃ tu rakṣāṃ gotraṃ ca nāma ca saṃkīrtanaṃ ca rāmasya sītāyāḥ prasavau śubhau
english: Even as that protective rite was being performed, along with the recitation of lineage and name, and the glorification of Rāma's name, came the auspicious birth-sons of Sītā.

sanskrit: ardharātre tu śatrughnaḥ śuśrāva sumahat priyam parṇaśālāṃ gato rātrau diṣṭyā diṣṭyeti cābravīt
english: At midnight, Śatrughna, who had gone to the leaf-hut that night, heard the most welcome of tidings; he exclaimed, "How fortunate! How fortunate!"

sanskrit: tatha tasya prahṛṣṭasya śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ vyatītā vārṣikī rātriḥ śrāvaṇī laghuvikramā
english: And for that great-souled, overjoyed Śatrughna, the rainy-season night of Śrāvaṇa, light of step, quickly passed.

sanskrit: prabhāte tu mahāvīryaḥ kṛtvā paurvāhṇikaṃ kramam muniṃ prāñjalir āmantrya prāyāt paścānmukhaḥ punaḥ
english: At dawn, the mighty hero completed his morning rituals, took leave of the sage with joined palms, and set out again, turning back westward.

sanskrit: sa gatvā yamunātīraṃ saptarātroṣitaḥ pathi ṛṣīṇāṃ puṇyakīrtīnām āśrame vāsam abhyayāt
english: Having journeyed to the bank of the Yamunā, he spent seven nights along the way, taking lodging in the hermitages of sages of holy renown.

sanskrit: sa tatra munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ bhārgavapramukhair nṛpaḥ kathābhir bahurūpābhir vāsaṃ cakre mahāyaśāḥ
english: There, together with the sages headed by Cyavana of the Bhārgava lineage, that greatly glorious king passed his time in many kinds of conversation.

sanskrit: atha rātryāṃ pravṛttāyāṃ śatrughno bhṛgunandanam papraccha cyavanaṃ vipraṃ lavaṇasya balābalam
english: When night had come, Śatrughna asked the brāhmaṇa Cyavana, joy of the Bhṛgu lineage, about the strength and weakness of Lavaṇa.

sanskrit: śūlasya ca balaṃ brahman ke ca pūrvaṃ nipātitāḥ anena śūlamukhena dvandvayuddham upāgatāḥ
english: "What is the power of his trident, O brāhmaṇa? Who before now have been slain — who came to single combat at the point of this trident?"

sanskrit: tasya tadbhāṣitaṃ śrutvā śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ pratyuvāca mahātejāś cyavano raghunandanam
english: Having heard those words of the great-souled Śatrughna, the mighty Cyavana replied to that scion of the Raghu line.

sanskrit: asaṃkhyeyāni karmāṇi yāny asya puruṣarṣabha ikṣvākuvaṃśaprabhave yad vṛttaṃ tac chṛṇuṣva me
english: "His deeds are beyond counting, O bull among men. Hear from me what transpired at the rise of the Ikṣvāku dynasty."

sanskrit: ayodhyāyāṃ purā rājā yuvanāśvasuto balī māndhātā iti vikhyātas triṣu lokeṣu vīryavān
english: "In Ayodhyā of old there was a mighty king, son of Yuvanāśva, renowned throughout the three worlds for his valor — known as Māndhātā."

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ śāsane pṛthivīpatiḥ suralokam atho jetum udyogam akaron nṛpaḥ
english: "Having brought the entire earth under his dominion, that lord of the earth, the king, undertook a campaign to conquer the world of the gods."

sanskrit: indrasya tu bhayaṃ tīvraṃ surāṇāṃ ca mahātmanām māndhātari kṛtodyoge devalokajigīṣayā
english: "When Māndhātā set out with desire to conquer the celestial world, Indra and all the great-souled gods were seized with intense fear."

sanskrit: ardhāsanena śakrasya rājyārdhena ca pārthivaḥ vandyamānaḥ suragaṇaiḥ pratijñām adhyarohata
english: "Honored by the host of gods with half of Indra's throne and half of his kingdom, that king of earth mounted a solemn pledge."

sanskrit: tasya pāpam abhiprāyaṃ viditvā pākaśāsanaḥ sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vākyam uvāca yuvanāśvajam
english: "Knowing his sinful intention, the chastiser of Pāka, Indra, spoke these appeasing words to the son of Yuvanāśva."

sanskrit: rājā tvaṃ mānuṣe loke na tāvat puruṣarṣabha akṛtvā pṛthivīṃ vaśyāṃ devarājyam ihecchasi
english: "'You are a king in the human world, O bull among men — you desire the kingdom of the gods here without yet having made the entire earth obedient to you.'"

sanskrit: yadi vīra samagrā te medinī nikhilā vaśe devarājyaṃ kuruṣveha sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ
english: "'If, O hero, the entire earth, whole and complete, is truly under your sway, then rule over the kingdom of the gods here, together with your troops, forces, and conveyances.'"

sanskrit: indram evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu māndhātā vākyam abravīt kva me śakra pratihataṃ śāsanaṃ pṛthivītale
english: "Then Māndhātā spoke these words to Indra as he spoke thus: 'Where on the face of the earth has my command been repelled, O Śakra?'"

sanskrit: tam uvāca sahasrākṣo lavaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ madhuputro madhuvane nājñāṃ te kurute 'nagha
english: "To him, the thousand-eyed one replied: 'Lavaṇa — a rākṣasa, son of Madhu, dwelling in the Madhu forest — does not observe your command, O sinless king.'"

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vipriyaṃ ghoraṃ sahasrākṣeṇa bhāṣitam vrīḍito 'vāṅmukho rājā vyāhartuṃ na śaśāka ha
english: "Hearing those harsh and unwelcome words spoken by Indra, the king was ashamed, bowed his head downward, and was unable to speak."

sanskrit: āmantrya tu sahasrākṣaṃ hriyā kiṃ cid avāṅmukhaḥ punar evāgamac chrīmān imaṃ lokaṃ nareśvaraḥ
english: "Taking leave of the thousand-eyed Indra, the glorious lord of men returned somewhat shame-faced to this world below."

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā hṛdaye 'marṣaṃ sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ ājagāma madhoḥ putraṃ vaśe kartum aninditaḥ
english: "Harboring indignation in his heart, that blameless one came with his troops, forces, and conveyances to bring the son of Madhu under his power."

sanskrit: sa kāṅkṣamāṇo lavaṇaṃ yuddhāya puruṣarṣabha dūtaṃ saṃpreṣayām āsa sakāśaṃ lavaṇasya saḥ
english: "Desiring to fight Lavaṇa, that bull among men dispatched a messenger to Lavaṇa's presence."

sanskrit: sa gatvā vipriyāṇy āha bahūni madhunaḥ sutam vadantam evaṃ taṃ dūtaṃ bhakṣayām āsa rākṣasaḥ
english: "The messenger went and spoke many harsh and unwelcome words to the son of Madhu; while speaking thus, that messenger was devoured by the rākṣasa."

sanskrit: cirāyamāṇe dūte tu rājā krodhasamanvitaḥ ardayām āsa tad rakṣaḥ śaravṛṣṭyā samantataḥ
english: "When the messenger was long delayed, the king, filled with wrath, assailed that rākṣasa on all sides with a shower of arrows."

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya lavaṇaḥ śūlaṃ jagrāha pāṇinā vadhāya sānubandhasya mumocāyudham uttamam
english: "Then Lavaṇa laughed aloud, took his trident in hand, and hurled that supreme weapon to slay the king along with all his followers."

sanskrit: tac chūlaṃ dīpyamānaṃ tu sabhṛtyabalavāhanam bhasmīkṛtya nṛpaṃ bhūyo lavaṇasyāgamat karam
english: "That blazing trident reduced the king, together with his troops, forces, and conveyances, to ashes, and then returned once more to the hand of Lavaṇa."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa rājā sumahān hataḥ sabalavāhanaḥ śūlasya ca balaṃ vīra aprameyam anuttamam
english: "In this manner that great king was slain together with his forces and conveyances. The power of the trident, O hero, is immeasurable and unsurpassed."

sanskrit: śvaḥ prabhāte tu lavaṇaṃ vadhiṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ agṛhītāyudhaṃ kṣipraṃ dhruvo hi vijayas tava
english: "Tomorrow at dawn you shall without doubt slay Lavaṇa — catch him quickly before he takes up his weapon; victory is then certain for you."

sanskrit: kathāṃ kathayatāṃ teṣāṃ jayaṃ cākāṅkṣatāṃ śubham vyatītā rajanī śīghraṃ śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ
english: As they conversed and eagerly awaited auspicious victory, the night passed quickly for that great-souled Śatrughna.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhāte vimale tasmin kāle sa rākṣasaḥ nirgatas tu purād vīro bhakṣāhārapracoditaḥ
english: Then, at that bright and clear dawn, the rākṣasa warrior went out from the city, driven by hunger in search of prey.

sanskrit: etasminn antare śūraḥ śatrughno yamunāṃ nadīm tīrtvā madhupuradvāri dhanuṣpāṇir atiṣṭhata
english: Meanwhile, the heroic Śatrughna crossed the river Yamunā and stood at the gate of Madhupura, bow in hand.

sanskrit: tato 'rdhadivase prāpte krūrakarmā sa rākṣasaḥ āgacchad bahusahasraṃ prāṇinām udvahan bharam
english: Then, when midday had arrived, that cruel-deeded rākṣasa came back, bearing the weight of many thousands of living creatures.

sanskrit: tato dadarśa śatrughnaṃ sthitaṃ dvāri dhṛtāyudham tam uvāca tato rakṣaḥ kim anena kariṣyasi
english: Then he saw Śatrughna standing at the gate, holding his weapon. The rākṣasa then said to him: "What will you do with this?"

sanskrit: īdṛśānāṃ sahasrāṇi sāyudhānāṃ narādhama bhakṣitāni mayā roṣāt kālam ākāṅkṣase nu kim
english: "Thousands like you, armed as you are, O basest of men, have been devoured by me in fury. Are you awaiting your appointed time?"

sanskrit: āhāraś cāpy asaṃpūrṇo mamāyaṃ puruṣādhama svayaṃ praviṣṭo nu mukhaṃ katham āsādya durmate
english: "My meal today is also not yet complete, O most despicable of men. How have you, having come on your own, walked into my very mouth, O fool?"

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ bhāṣamāṇasya hasataś ca muhur muhuḥ śatrughno vīryasaṃpanno roṣād aśrūṇy avartayat
english: As he spoke thus and laughed again and again, Śatrughna, full of valor, shed tears of rage.

sanskrit: tasya roṣābhibhūtasya śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ tejomayā marīcyas tu sarvagātrair viniṣpatan
english: From that great-souled Śatrughna, overcome by rage, rays of fiery energy blazed forth from every limb of his body.

sanskrit: uvāca ca susaṃkruddhaḥ śatrughnas taṃ niśācaram yoddhum icchāmi durbuddhe dvandvayuddhaṃ tvayā saha
english: And Śatrughna, deeply enraged, said to that night-wanderer: "I wish to fight you in single combat, O evil-minded one."

sanskrit: putro daśarathasyāhaṃ bhrātā rāmasya dhīmataḥ śatrughno nāma śatrughno vadhākāṅkṣī tavāgataḥ
english: "I am the son of Daśaratha, the brother of the wise Rāma. My name is Śatrughna — Śatrughna, come here desiring your death."

sanskrit: tasya me yuddhakāmasya dvandvayuddhaṃ pradīyatām śatrus tvaṃ sarvajīvānāṃ na me jīvan gamiṣyasi
english: "Let single combat be granted to me who desire battle. You are the enemy of all living beings — you shall not escape me alive."

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā bruvāṇe tu rākṣasaḥ prahasann iva pratyuvāca naraśreṣṭhaṃ diṣṭyā prāpto 'si durmate
english: While he spoke thus, the rākṣasa laughed aloud and replied to that foremost of men: "By good fortune you have come, O fool."

sanskrit: mama mātṛṣvasur bhrātā rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ hato rāmeṇa durbuddhe strīhetoḥ puruṣādhama
english: "My mother's sister's brother — the rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa — was slain by Rāma, O evil-minded one, for the sake of a woman, O basest of men."

sanskrit: tac ca sarvaṃ mayā kṣāntaṃ rāvaṇasya kulakṣayam avajñāṃ purataḥ kṛtvā mayā yūyaṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: "All of that — the destruction of Rāvaṇa's clan — I have endured, keeping contempt before me, especially toward you and your kind."

sanskrit: na hatāś ca hi me sarve paribhūtās tṛṇaṃ yathā bhūtāś caiva bhaviṣyāś ca yūyaṃ ca puruṣādhamāḥ
english: "All of you have not been slain — you are despised like blades of grass — those who exist, those who shall exist, and you too, O basest of men."

sanskrit: tasya te yuddhakāmasya yuddhaṃ dāsyāmi durmate īpsitaṃ yādṛśaṃ tubhyaṃ sajjaye yāvad āyudham
english: "To you who desire battle I shall give battle, O fool — the kind you desire — wait while I make ready my weapon."

sanskrit: tam uvācātha śatrughnaḥ kva me jīvan gamiṣyasi durbalo 'py āgataḥ śatrur na moktavyaḥ kṛtātmanā
english: Then Śatrughna said to him: "Where will you go from me alive? Even a weakened enemy who has come must not be released by a man of steadfast soul."

sanskrit: yo hi viklavayā buddhyā prasaraṃ śatrave dadau sa hato mandabuddhitvād yathā kāpuruṣas tathā
english: "For he who, with a confused mind, gives an enemy room to maneuver is destroyed by his own weak-mindedness, like a coward."
